earlier_scan.source_named: Boyd, Virginia L. 1997. A Phonology and Grammar of Mbodomo. MA thesis, University of Texas at Arlington (per Glottolog/WALS refdb 1235; no fulltext located).

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Mbodomo (wals code mdo); all 34 datapoints cite Boyd 1997.
sources.note: No stress features (14A-17A / StressTyp) coded for Mbodomo; only 10A/10B nasal vowels from phonology.

sources.citation: Boyd, Virginia Lee. 1997. A Phonology and Grammar of Mbódɔ́mɔ́. MA thesis, University of Texas at Arlington. xv+221 pp. (SIL REAP scan, 236 PDF pp; archived copy (Internet Archive, 8 Dec 2023) of sil.org/system/files/reapdata/; text layer is a -1-shifted font, decoded to)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online
sources.note: Nothing. Ch.2 Phonology (pp.9-60) covers consonants, vowels, syllable structure (2.3; 2.3.1 'The vowel is the tone-bearing unit', p.28) and 2.4 Tone (pp.41-49: two lexical tones H/L on nouns/modifiers; verbs lexically toneless with a fixed H-L melody in isolation; downdrift; grammatical tone: L-dissimilation, person marking by verb tone). Full-text search of the whole thesis: zero occurrences of 'stress'; 'accent' only in 'accentuates'; 'intonation' only re question intonation (p.166). No statement on word stress/accent.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Section 3 'Le ton' (p.18ff): 'La langue mbodomo a deux tons de base, ton haut.. et ton bas'; six word tone melodies after Moñino 1995:123; lexical tone on non-verbs, verbs carry only aspectual tone. 'accent' used only for orthographic diacritics (accent aigu/grave).
